distros.debian: git clone https://github.com/pwndbg/pwndbg && cd pwndbg && ./setup.sh
distros.git: git clone https://github.com/pwndbg/pwndbg && cd pwndbg && ./setup.sh

notes: De facto standard for binary exploitation CTFs and zero-day exploit research.

name: Angr
tagline: Powerful Python framework for symbolic execution and automated binary analysis
purpose_summary: Solve CTF crackmes, reverse engineer obfuscated binaries, and find crash states automatically through symbolic execution without manually stepping through code.

distros.debian: pipx install angr || pip install angr
distros.git: git clone https://github.com/angr/angr.git && cd angr && pip install -e .

quick_commands.label: Python Symbolic Path Explorer
quick_commands.cmd: python3 -c "import angr; p = angr.Project('./binary'); sm = p.factory.simulation_manager(); sm.explore(find=0x401234, avoid=0x401250); print(sm.found[0].posix.dumps(0))"

notes: Developed by the Computer Security Lab at UC Santa Barbara. Mind-blowing for automatically finding winning program paths.

name: ROPgadget
tagline: Search for gadgets in binaries and automatically generate ROP chains
purpose_summary: Scan ELF, PE, and Mach-O binaries to find Return-Oriented Programming (ROP) gadgets and generate automated execve / shellcode execution chains.

distros.debian: sudo apt install python3-ropgadget -y || pip install ropgadget
distros.git: git clone https://github.com/JonathanSalwan/ROPgadget.git && cd ROPgadget && pip install .

notes: Essential for bypassing W^X, NX-bit, and Data Execution Prevention (DEP).

name: Volatility 3
tagline: Advanced memory forensics framework for Windows, Linux & macOS RAM dumps
purpose_summary: Analyze RAM memory captures, uncover injected DLLs, recover lost passwords, list rogue processes, extract network sockets, and investigate malware in memory.

distros.debian: sudo apt install python3-pip -y && pip install volatility3
distros.git: git clone https://github.com/volatilityfoundation/volatility3.git && cd volatility3 && pip install .

notes: Python 3 rewrite with automatic symbol server integration—no more manually finding kernel profiles!

name: RegRipper
tagline: Targeted Windows registry hive forensic analysis tool
purpose_summary: Extract timestamped forensic artifacts, user activity, mounted USB devices, recently executed programs, and network history from extracted Windows registry hives.

distros.debian: sudo apt install libparse-win32registry-perl -y && git clone https://github.com/keydet89/RegRipper3.0.git
distros.git: git clone https://github.com/keydet89/RegRipper3.0.git && cd RegRipper3.0

quick_commands.label: Rip SYSTEM Hive for USB Devices

notes: Created by DFIR veteran Harlan Carvey. Uses plugins to extract high-value forensic timelines.

name: ScareCrow
tagline: Payload creation framework designed to bypass EDR and AV sensors
purpose_summary: Package raw shellcode into legitimate-looking Windows signed binaries (DLL, CPL, EXE) utilizing unhooking, AMSI/ETW patching, and binary sign spoofing.

distros.debian: sudo apt install -y openssl golang osslsigncode mingw-w64 && git clone https://github.com/optiv/ScareCrow.git && cd ScareCrow && go build ScareCrow.go
distros.git: git clone https://github.com/optiv/ScareCrow.git && cd ScareCrow && go build ScareCrow.go

research_links.title: Optiv Blog - ScareCrow EDR Bypass Release

quick_commands.label: Compile DLL with AMSI Bypass & Signing

notes: Uses syscall unhooking, custom sleep timers, and code-signing forgery to slip past top-tier EDRs.

name: SysWhispers3
tagline: AV/EDR evasion via direct system calls in C/C++ payloads
purpose_summary: Generate C and ASM stubs for direct system calls, bypassing user-mode API hooking deployed by modern EDRs on NTDLL.dll functions.

distros.debian: git clone https://github.com/klezVirus/SysWhispers3.git && cd SysWhispers3 && pip install -r requirements.txt
distros.git: git clone https://github.com/klezVirus/SysWhispers3.git && cd SysWhispers3 && pip install -r requirements.txt

research_links.title: Medium - Evading EDR with SysWhispers3 Direct Syscalls

notes: Supports x64 and WOW64 with multiple recovery methods (Jumper, Egg Hunter, Direct, Hell's Gate / Halo's Gate).

name: Hashcat
tagline: World's fastest and most advanced GPU-accelerated password recovery engine
purpose_summary: Crack password hashes (NTLM, NetNTLMv2, Kerberos, WPA2/WPA3, MD5, SHA256, bcrypt) utilizing GPU compute acceleration and custom rule engines.

distros.debian: sudo apt install hashcat -y
distros.git: git clone https://github.com/hashcat/hashcat.git && cd hashcat && make && sudo make install

notes: Supports OpenCL, CUDA, and Metal acceleration. Over 400 hash modes supported.

name: John the Ripper
tagline: Feature-rich password cracker with auto-detection of hash algorithms and formats
purpose_summary: Crack encrypted archives (zip, rar, 7z), SSH keys, keepass databases, and /etc/shadow hashes with automated hash format recognition.

distros.debian: sudo apt install john -y
distros.git: git clone https://github.com/openwall/john.git && cd john/src && ./configure && make

notes: Includes famous *2john helpers: zip2john, rar2john, ssh2john, keepass2john, 7z2john.

name: CloudFox
tagline: Command line tool to find actionable attack paths in cloud infrastructure
purpose_summary: Analyze AWS and Azure environments after acquiring initial credentials, finding high-value attack paths, exposed databases, privileged IAM roles, and secrets.

distros.debian: wget https://github.com/BishopFox/cloudfox/releases/latest/download/cloudfox-linux-amd64.tar.gz && tar -zxvf cloudfox-linux-amd64.tar.gz && sudo mv cloudfox /usr/local/bin/
distros.git: git clone https://github.com/BishopFox/cloudfox.git && cd cloudfox && go build

notes: Created by BishopFox specifically to avoid information overload during cloud pentests by pinpointing exploitable paths directly.

name: Kube-hunter
tagline: Hunt for security weaknesses and misconfigurations in Kubernetes clusters
purpose_summary: Actively probe Kubernetes clusters for exposed API servers, kubelet read-only ports, etcd open access, SSRF to cloud metadata, and container breakout points.

distros.debian: pipx install kube-hunter || pip install kube-hunter
distros.git: git clone https://github.com/aquasecurity/kube-hunter.git && cd kube-hunter && pip install -r requirements.txt

notes: Supports passive, active, and internal pod-based scanning modes.

name: Pacu
tagline: The AWS exploitation framework for red teams
purpose_summary: Perform post-compromise AWS exploitation with modules for privilege escalation, IAM persistence, CloudTrail disruption, and Lambda data exfiltration.

distros.debian: pipx install pacu || pip install pacu
distros.git: git clone https://github.com/RhinoSecurityLabs/pacu.git && cd pacu && pip3 install -r requirements.txt

quick_commands.label: Run IAM Privesc Scanner Inside Pacu

notes: The Metasploit of AWS cloud penetration testing.

name: Binwalk
tagline: Firmware analysis, extraction, and reverse engineering engine
purpose_summary: Analyze embedded firmware binary images, identify file systems (SquashFS, CramFS, JFFS2), extract compressed files, and uncover hidden crypto keys.

distros.debian: sudo apt install binwalk -y
distros.git: git clone https://github.com/ReFirmLabs/binwalk.git && cd binwalk && sudo python3 setup.py install

research_links.title: Medium - Extracting IoT Secrets with Binwalk

notes: Essential first step in any IoT, router, IP camera, or automotive embedded pentest.

name: EMBA
tagline: The security analyzer for embedded Linux firmware
purpose_summary: Completely automated security testing suite for embedded device firmware; extracts, identifies hardcoded credentials, outdated software, CVEs, and binaries with weak protections.

distros.debian: git clone https://github.com/e-m-b-a/emba.git && cd emba && sudo ./installer.sh -d
distros.git: git clone https://github.com/e-m-b-a/emba.git && cd emba && sudo ./installer.sh -F

research_links.title: Medium - Automated Firmware Pentesting with EMBA

notes: Rare and exceptionally deep firmware auditing suite with an HTML reporting dashboard output.

name: Routersploit
tagline: The automated exploitation framework for embedded devices and routers
purpose_summary: Exploit embedded routers, IP webcams, and smart IoT devices using a modular Metasploit-like framework with automated vulnerability scanner modules.

distros.debian: sudo apt install routersploit -y || git clone https://github.com/threat9/routersploit && cd routersploit && pip3 install -r requirements.txt
distros.git: git clone https://github.com/threat9/routersploit.git && cd routersploit && pip3 install -r requirements.txt

quick_commands.label: Run AutoPwn Scanner on Target IP
quick_commands.cmd:
rsf.py
use scanners/autopwn
set target 192.168.1.1
run

notes: Includes hundreds of exploits for Netgear, Cisco, D-Link, Huawei, TP-Link, and Linksys devices.
